brief:
A former senior official at the UN World Food Programme has launched an appeal against his dismissal, alleging the agency terminated him in retaliation for his public statements on famine conditions in Gaza, Al-Monitor reported. The case has surfaced internal tensions within the UN organization over how it addresses humanitarian crises and staff advocacy.

The ex-director's challenge comes as the WFP faces mounting criticism over its handling of the Gaza humanitarian emergency and questions about the independence of its workforce in addressing food security issues in conflict zones.
dek: By Emma Farge and Crispian Balmer GENEVA/ROME, Oct 2 (Reuters) - A former senior UN food agency official has said he has launched an appeal against his dismissal, alleging it was motivated by his stance on hunger in Gaza, in a case that has exposed tensions…
title: Fired UN food official challenges dismissal over Gaza hunger stance
